summary: Coordination provides a partial receiver admission precursor with copied input bytes, immutable transcript snapshots, purpose-bound pending challenges and no-effect reducers. At 791bd37, direct journal staging could discard or replace a pending challenge without recording its disposition; the earlier claim that staging preserved challenge history was too broad. The repair at f934aad1 requires the entire pending challenge to remain unchanged or its exact ID/digest to enter the consumed/abandoned ledger before staging. Regression tests cover drop, replacement, mutation, wrong ID/digest and epoch changes, requiring refusal, byte-identical journal preservation, restored pending state and no runner calls; exact retention and both dispositions remain accepted. PR #998 merged at 9ab0b8c652ac3ad745991a4c3acb64b593b6d0c0 after hosted compiler-and-tests and coherent aggregate checks passed for f934aad1 (https://github.com/FS-GG/FS.GG.Coordination/actions/runs/38793161044 and https://github.com/FS-GG/FS.GG.Coordination/actions/runs/38793161293). Source-only v2 drafts share the existing journal key/lock, retain v1 readers, original pins and holds, and count duplicated pinned/event bytes and pending challenge bytes toward the transcript cap; serialized supplier records have a separate cap. Staging and restart still report durability Unknown; ACK preparation and production host handoff always refuse. The injected source adapter supplies interpreted claims rather than a qualified exact-envelope authenticator. Exact-envelope provenance and original-byte joins, ACK checkpoint semantics, durable crash-cut admission, once-only production handoff and complete replay/v1 matrices remain open. This source repair and passing hosted checks do not establish an authenticated unattended host endpoint, installed allocation/launch/teardown, worker-loss recovery, native acceptance or retirement of earlier operations; those acceptance boundaries remain held.
title: V3 receiver admission draft is inert source, not installed authority
